inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2026 cash-flow statement add-back 'Stock compensation' $237M (FY2025 $263M, FY2024 $260M). Cash tax withholding on net-share settlement is not disclosed separately by Emerson (it nets inside 'Other, net' financing, -$111M in FY26 with other items) and no company combined figure exists, so the add-back is used unadjusted.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 financing outflow 'Purchases of common stock' $1,000M (7.2M shares at $139.29 average); FY2025 $1,167M. FY2027 outlook assumes ~$2.5B of repurchases. The flat count is funded: buybacks run 4x SBC or more and the weighted diluted count has fallen 574.0M (FY24) -> 566.7M (FY25) -> 562.0M (FY26).
inputs.fy0_basis: FY0 is now FY2026 ACTUAL (year ended 2026-09-30, 10-K filed November 2026), replacing the FY2026E guidance-based FY0 of the 2026-09-28 version. Year 1 of the build is FY2027 in both versions, so the horizon did not roll - only the FY0 estimates were replaced by actuals. Revenue $18,982M (+5.4% reported, +4% underlying); continuing-operations OCF $3,978M less capex $443M = reported FCF $3,535M (the prior version carried the ~$3.6B guide; the print was ~$65M light on a $338M operating-working-capital build, mostly inventory). Balance sheet and FY0 flows now share one date, so the prior version's uncredited Q4 FY26 cash is now inside net debt.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at the balance-sheet date: 557.3M common shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (10-K balance sheet) + 2.4M dilutive shares (FY26 EPS reconciliation: diluted 562.0M less basic 559.6M) = 559.7M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). NOT used: the 10-K cover reports 548.6M shares outstanding at 2026-10-31, 8.7M below the September count. The filing text gives no accelerated-repurchase or subsequent-event disclosure explaining it; if it is an October repurchase under the FY27 ~$2.5B plan it came with roughly $1.3-1.4B of cash out that is not in the 2026-09-30 net debt, so taking the lower count without the higher debt would overstate value by ~$2/share. Count and net debt are kept on the same date; revisit at the Q1 FY27 10-Q.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), beta ~1.1, ERP ~4.5-5% -> cost of equity ~9.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (A-rated; commercial paper at 3.9% at year end, 2025 notes at 3.0-5.0%), ~3.5% after tax; capital structure ~88% equity (~$90.7B market cap) / 12% debt ($12.2B) -> WACC ~8.4-8.6%. 8.5% used in ALL scenarios: risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into per-scenario discount rates (adaptations item f). UNCHANGED from 2026-09-28.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. US GAAP ASC 842 operating lease cost is already inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities ($694M at 2026-09-30) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required. NCI is $16M at 2026-09-30 after the March 2025 buyout of the remaining AspenTech shares; NCI share of FY26 earnings was $2M. Flows are effectively 100% attributable.
inputs.da_treatment: da_pct_path is the CASH-TAX-DEDUCTIBLE D&A only: depreciation ($362M FY26, 1.9% of revenue) plus capitalized-software amortization ($103M) plus the deductible slice of intangibles amortization. Total GAAP D&A is $1,478M (7.8%) because $1,013M/yr of acquired-intangible amortization from the NI (FY24) and AspenTech stock deals is non-cash AND largely non-deductible (FY26 income taxes paid $960M vs $796M book expense). A non-cash, non-deductible charge has zero FCF effect, so it is left out of the build rather than modelled with a phantom tax shield that would then be perpetuated in the terminal value. Cash tax rate (22%) is applied to EBIT after deductible D&A only: FY26 check - taxes paid $960M + interest shield ~$73M = $1,033M on (EBITDA post-SBC $5,301M - deductible D&A ~$760M) = 22.7%. Deductible amortization fades from ~2.1% to ~1.1% of revenue as older layers roll off. UNCHANGED.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing row: operating company, cyclical industrial -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations for leases/NCI/charging risk once). Same model as the 2026-09-28 first valuation; this is an UPDATE to FY2026 actuals and the FY2027 outlook. EBITDA margin path is company-level EBITDA BEFORE SBC and AFTER restructuring and acquisition/divestiture fees (treated as recurring). FY2026 actual: pretax $3,489M + net interest $334M + D&A $1,478M = $5,301M post-SBC, + SBC $237M = $5,538M = 29.2% of sales as reported; excluding the one-off IEEPA tariff refund net of the charitable-trust contribution ($91M) it is $5,447M = 28.7% - slightly below the 29.0% the prior version assumed for FY26E. FY2027 outlook (sales ~+5% reported and underlying, GAAP EPS ~$5.70 vs $4.79, adjusted EPS ~$7.25 vs $6.59, OCF $4.3-4.4B, capex ~$0.5B, FCF $3.8-3.9B, restructuring ~$0.14/share vs $0.36) implies pre-SBC EBITDA of roughly 30.5% on the EPS bridge, but the FCF guide implies continued cash leakage (working capital, restructuring cash, pension) - the base year-1 margin of 29.7% with a -15% working-capital capture is calibrated to the CASH guide: engine year-1 unlevered owner FCF of ~$3.96B vs guide-implied ~$3.86B (FCF midpoint $3,850M + after-tax net interest ~$257M - SBC ~$245M). The $10.4B net debt is deducted separately. METRICS CSV: the quarter-label fix in EMR_Metrics.csv (rows previously shifted one quarter early) changes NO driver - the 2026-09-28 build had already anchored on XBRL period dates rather than CSV labels, and every anchor here is read from the FY2026 10-K text. The CSV has no FY2026 annual row yet (XBRL frames lag), so the workbook's Actuals sheet stops at FY2025; FY2026 figures in this file come from EMR_Annual_FY2026.txt. Safety & Productivity ($2,174M sales, 11.5% of revenue, adjusted EBITA $471M per the FY26 segment note; the prior version's '~$1.4B / 8%' was wrong) is NOT carved out: the FY2026 10-K text carries no strategic-review or held-for-sale language for it, and a sale at fair value would be roughly value-neutral. Historical CAGRs are heavily distorted by the portfolio transformation and are reported but not used as the growth anchor.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management FY2027 outlook (net and underlying sales ~+5%), backlog $9,593M at 2026-09-30 (+11% YoY; ~70% converts within 12 months) and the mid-single-digit through-cycle organic target. Historical CAGRs are not usable as the anchor (see notes).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 15.9% vs revenue 5yr 8.0% and EPS 5yr 4.6%; equity 3yr -7.9% vs revenue 3yr +7.8%: divergence >30% in both windows. Equity was inflated by the FY2023 Copeland gain ($13.2B net income) and then cut by the $7.2B AspenTech minority buyout booked through equity in FY2025. Flagged; equity CAGR not used.
historical_growth.notes: Windows now end at FY2026 (FY2023->FY2026 and FY2021->FY2026) using the FY2026 10-K; the prior version's windows ended at FY2025, which is why every figure moved - none of the change is due to the CSV quarter-label fix, which touched only quarterly rows. Revenue FY21 $12,932M and FY23 $15,165M are continuing-operations restated bases, so both revenue CAGRs embed the NI acquisition (FY24) and are not organic (underlying growth was 3-4% in FY25-26). EPS 3yr is measured off FY2023's $22.88, which is the Copeland gain. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not stripped: net-debt company). Series (USD m): FY21 2,947; FY22 2,479; FY23 3 (OCF hit by divestiture taxes - the 3yr CAGR off this base is not meaningful and is left null); FY24 2,638 continuing; FY25 2,982 continuing (2,404 total incl. -$578M discontinued-ops tax); FY26 3,298. SBC-adjusted and reported 5yr FCF CAGRs now coincide (2.3% vs 2.2%) because SBC fell to $237M in FY26, back near its FY21 level of $224M; the prior concern that SBC was outgrowing cash flow has eased.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 at 5.0% = the FY2027 outlook (was 5.5%). FY28 5.5% retained: backlog +11% to $9.6B with ~30% converting beyond 12 months, Software & Systems underlying +7% and Test & Measurement +15% in FY26. FY29-36 UNCHANGED, fading to 2.5% as the LNG/power project cycle matures.
base.margin_rationale: FY27 29.7% (was 29.0%): FY26 printed 28.7% clean, and the FY27 outlook adds ~1pt from adjusted-EBITA expansion (adjusted EPS +10% on sales +5%) and lower restructuring, held ~0.8pt below the EPS-implied ~30.5% so that year-1 cash ties to the FCF guide. Mature level 30.5% from FY33 UNCHANGED; FY28-FY31 lifted 0.1-0.6pt only to keep the path monotonic from the higher start - the ramp is now slower (+0.1-0.2pt/yr), not higher.
base.wc_rationale: Operating working capital rose to 11.9% of sales (FY25 11.3%, FY24 8.0%); the FY26 build was $338M on a $966M revenue increase and FY25+FY26 together consumed 23% of the revenue increase. Capture moved from -12% to -15% (above the steady-state ~12% level ratio, below the two-year 23% which includes an inventory build). Sign negative per the manufacturer rule.

bull.growth_rationale: UNCHANGED. Top of the 4-7% organic band plus pricing: AI data-centre on-site power, Ovation/power demand, the LNG funnel and the semiconductor and aerospace T&M recovery (T&M underlying +15% in FY26) all running concurrently for 3-4 years - a beat-and-raise against the ~5% FY27 outlook.
bull.margin_rationale: FY27-FY30 lifted (30.3/30.6/30.9/31.2 vs 29.5/30.0/30.5/31.0) so the bull starts above the new base; the 32% mature level from FY32 is UNCHANGED - best-in-class, above any automation peer.

bear.growth_rationale: UNCHANGED. The FY27 outlook explicitly 'assumes the impact of the Middle East conflict is contained within the region'; the bear is that it is not, on top of China (-7% underlying in FY26) and an FY28-29 industrial-capex downturn: FY27 +2% against the +5% guide, revenue -3% at the FY29 trough, recovery to ~3% and fade to 2%.
bear.margin_rationale: UNCHANGED. FY27 28.0% is a miss against both the FY26 clean 28.7% and the outlook; volume deleverage takes company EBITDA to 26% at the trough, recovering only to 28% as the software mix shift stalls. Pillar 2 lifts the cash tax rate to 23%.

scenario_narratives.base: Emerson closed FY2026 at $19.0B of sales (+4% underlying), a 26.6% adjusted EBITA margin and a record $9.6B backlog (+11%), and guides FY2027 to ~5% growth, adjusted EPS ~$7.25 and FCF of $3.8-3.9B. Base takes the guide for FY27, 5.5% in FY28 on backlog conversion, then fades growth to 2.5% by FY36, while software mix (Software & Systems is a third of sales and growing 7-8%) and NI/AspenTech synergies carry company EBITDA from 29.7% to 30.5%. China (-7%) and the Middle East drag (~1pt of FY26 sales) are not assumed to reverse. Non-deductible acquisition amortization is left out of the build (no cash, no shield). Buybacks fund a flat share count; net debt of $10.4B (2.0x EBITDA) is deducted once. The axes that matter are (1) whether backlog converts at software-like margins AND into cash - FY26 FCF was a touch light on an inventory build - and (2) whether the hardware half (Intelligent Devices, 55% of sales, +3% underlying on price with flat volume) stays above trough through the next capex cycle.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI/data-centre power buildout, the LNG funnel and the semiconductor and aerospace test recovery run concurrently for 3-4 years, lifting growth to 7-7.5% - a sustained beat of the ~5% FY27 outlook - and pulling AspenTech/DeltaV software toward 40%+ of revenue. Company EBITDA reaches 32%, a level no automation peer has achieved, which is why this is the bull and not the base. A Safety & Productivity sale at a full multiple would be upside on top (not modelled). Terminal growth 3.0%, cap 20x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Middle East conflict is not contained (the FY27 outlook assumes it is), China stays in decline, and an FY28-29 industrial-capex recession (oil/chemicals overcapacity, trade retaliation, financing-cost-driven project deferrals) follows. FY27 misses the guide at +2%, revenue falls 3% at the trough, EBITDA deleverages to 26%, and the recovery is muted because software growth stalls and NI synergies disappoint. Leverage at 2.0x means no solvency risk, but $3.9B of commercial paper must be rolled or termed out. Terminal growth 2.0%, cap 15x. The bear does not hit the zero floor - the business remains a ~$3B FCF generator throughout.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED from 2026-09-28. House default is 15/50/35. Bear held at 20%: the live headwinds are still there in the FY2026 10-K - the Middle East conflict (about 1pt of FY26 sales, and the FY27 outlook is explicitly conditional on it staying contained), China (-7% underlying), trade policy, and a hardware half still tied to oil/chemicals capex - so a mid-decade downturn is a normal outcome for this business, not a tail. Bull held at 30% because it needs three cycles (power, LNG, semis) to overlap AND margins to reach a level (32%) above every peer. No going-concern or single-customer risk, so bear is not pushed higher. What would move them: a contained-conflict assumption failing or an order decline would lift bear; two consecutive quarters of underlying growth above 7% with margin expansion would lift bull.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF, SBC fully expensed, share count flat and funded by buybacks, net debt of $10.4B deducted once at the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. The build is unlevered and uses only cash-tax-deductible D&A so the ~$1.0B/yr of non-deductible acquired-intangible amortization creates neither a phantom tax shield nor a fake cost. The market pays ~31x EV/owner-FCF (trailing), ~22x FY27 adjusted EPS and ~28x FY27 GAAP EPS for Emerson's software re-rating; at an 8.5% WACC the house basis says that price sits above even the bull case. A quality compounder that is not cheap. This update replaced guidance-based FY0 anchors with FY2026 actuals and re-judged only the FY2027 guidance year (growth, margin, capex), the SBC anchor and the working-capital capture; WACC, terminal assumptions, weights, tax, D&A, later-year growth and the mature margin levels are deliberately unchanged.
unchanged_and_what_would_move_it: WACC 8.5%, terminal growth 2.0/2.5/3.0%, cap multiples 15/18/20x: would move on a sustained shift in the 10y UST of ~1pt or a change in leverage policy (e.g. a levered acquisition).
Growth FY28-FY36 in all scenarios, and FY27 in bull and bear: would move on FY27 order and backlog trends diverging from the ~5% outlook for two or more quarters.
Mature EBITDA margin 30.5% base / 32% bull / 28% bear: would move if adjusted segment EBITA expansion stalls below ~27.5% in FY27 or clears ~29% ahead of schedule.
Cash tax 22% (23% bear) on EBIT after deductible D&A: FY26 cash taxes of $960M back-solve to 22.7%; would move on a disclosed change in amortization deductibility or Pillar 2 top-up.
Deductible D&A path and scenario weights 20/50/30.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value carries most of the EV: a 1pp move in WACC or terminal growth swings value ~15-20% (see sensitivity grid).

EBITDA margin is derived from GAAP pretax + interest + D&A, not a company-reported total-company EBITDA; a ~1pp error in the FY27 starting margin is ~$8/share. The EPS guide implies ~30.5% against the 29.7% used; the gap is deliberate (cash calibration) and worth ~$5-6/share of conservatism if FY27 cash conversion comes in clean.

Share count: the 10-K cover shows 548.6M shares at 2026-10-31 vs 557.3M at 2026-09-30 with no explanatory disclosure; the model keeps count and net debt on 2026-09-30. Repurchases at ~$160 against a house value near $120 destroy a little value per remaining share rather than add it.

The cash tax treatment (22% on EBIT after deductible D&A only) is a judgment on how much of the ~$1.0B amortization is deductible; if more is deductible than assumed, value is understated by up to ~$5/share.
FY26 FCF ($3,535M) came in below the ~$3.6B guide on an inventory build; a second year of working-capital leakage above the -15% capture would cut year-1 cash by ~$100-200M.
~$3.9B of commercial paper (3.9% at year end) is short-dated; refinancing at 5%+ raises interest (outside the unlevered build but a real equity cost).
